message:
Hint sequential access when loading RDB and AOF files (#15782)

RDB and AOF file loading reads the file sequentially through small
reads. On storage with non-trivial latency (e.g. EBS) the load is
bounded by the kernel's default 128 KB read-ahead window rather than by
the disk or the CPU. `POSIX_FADV_SEQUENTIAL` doubles that window for the
file, provides faster RDB and AOF loading on EBS alike disks.

**RDB**

| dataset | x86-64 before | x86-64 after | change | aarch64 before |
aarch64 after | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128 B strings, 20M keys | 17.3 s | 15.2 s | -12% | 17.5 s | 16.8 s |
-4% |
| 256 B strings, 10M | 12.6 s | 10.6 s | -16% | 11.9 s | 10.5 s | -12% |
| 512 B strings, 5M | 9.3 s | 7.6 s | -18% | 8.5 s | 7.1 s | -17% |
| 1 KB strings, 2.5M | 7.4 s | 6.0 s | -19% | 6.6 s | 5.4 s | -18% |
| 4 KB strings, 700K | 6.7 s | 5.4 s | -19% | 5.8 s | 4.7 s | -19% |
| 32 KB strings, 90K | 6.3 s | 5.1 s | -20% | 5.4 s | 4.3 s | -20% |

**AOF** (plain text SET commands)

| dataset | x86-64 before | x86-64 after | change | aarch64 before |
aarch64 after | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128 B values, 10M | 11.4 s | 9.5 s | -17% | 11.3 s | 10.2 s | -10% |
| 256 B values, 6M | 10.3 s | 8.2 s | -20% | 9.9 s | 8.0 s | -19% |
| 1 KB values, 1.8M | 9.4 s | 7.0 s | -25% | 8.7 s | 6.6 s | -24% |
| 4 KB values, 500K | 9.5 s | 7.0 s | -26% | 8.7 s | 6.5 s | -26% |

No change when the file is already in the page cache. No change with 1
MB values either: each value is read with one large read, so the
read-ahead window does not matter there.

**Further improvement, outside Redis:** the kernel limits how far ahead
it reads a file with `/sys/block/<dev>/queue/read_ahead_kb` (default
128). The hint above can only double that limit. Raising the setting
itself (e.g. to 1024) removes the disk from the picture entirely:
loading from disk then takes the same time as loading a file already in
memory.

**Further improvement, in Redis:** We may implement readhead which will
could call `posix_fadvise()` for the next a few MBs of pages. We
experimented with it, there was no downside that we are aware of.
Though, we are not sure if there could be some side effects on some
setup. e.g. frequent `posix_fadvise()` syscalls may bring some overhead.
We are leaving this option out of this PR's scope to experiment with it
later.
